newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait concerned over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait concerned over U.S. vote on Jerusalem.

text.p: Kuwait on Sunday voiced concern over a U.S. House of Representatives recommendation to President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
"The cabinet has expressed regret and concern" over the resolution, a cabinet statement said.

"The resolution represents a hindrance to the (Arab-Israeli) peace process and a violation to the accords reached under the framework of that process," said the statement issued after a regular cabinet meeting.
Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed Tuesday's 406-17 vote.
The Palestinians, who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, have termed the resolution, which does not oblige the U.S. administration to act, a declaration of war.

In October 1995, the Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and that the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.
But recognising the volatility of the issue of Jerusalem, it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
Costa Rica and El Salvador are the only countries with embassies in Jerusalem.
